thread:
nina: Heads-up — CI started failing with 401s on the SDK e2e on mac runners. Quick check: anyone seen API key envs carrying a stray newline that breaks Basic auth headers?
alex: yep, seen that. usually from reading a file with a trailing newline and then doing `export REDWOOD_KEY=$(cat keyfile)` or passing it into Docker build args without trimming.
sam: fwiw mac `base64` can wrap lines which makes a `Authorization: Basic ...` header wrong if you base64 the credentials locally and paste them. use `base64` flags to avoid wrapping.
nina: exact error in logs was `401 Authorization failed` right when the streaming socket negotiated. curl with `-v` showed header had a `\n` inside the value.
maya: quick fixes: `export REDWOOD_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n' < keyfile)` or `export REDWOOD_KEY=$(printf '%s' "$(cat keyfile)")` — both strip trailing newline.
alex: for Docker builds: bad pattern `docker build --build-arg API_KEY="$(cat keyfile)" .` will include newline. instead do `docker build --build-arg API_KEY="$(tr -d '\r\n' < keyfile)" .` or write the key into a .env and `--env-file` for runtime only.
sam: if you base64 encode for Basic auth, on mac: `base64` wraps every 76 chars by default. do `base64 -b 0` (BSD) or `base64 --wrap=0` (GNU) to get single-line. e.g. `echo -n ":$REDWOOD_KEY" | base64 -b 0`
maya: another quick one for GH Actions: `echo "$KEY" >> $GITHUB_ENV` preserves newline. use `echo -n "$KEY" >> $GITHUB_ENV` or `printf '%s' "$KEY" >> $GITHUB_ENV` to avoid it.
ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: build #432 failed on e2e (401) — root cause suspected: API_KEY file had trailing CRLF from windows editor.
nina: 👌 repro steps I used: created keyfile with `printf '%s\r\n' 'abcd1234' > keyfile` then `export REDWOOD_KEY=$(cat keyfile)` and `curl -u :$REDWOOD_KEY https://api.redwood.example/v1/engines` -> 401.
alex: fix I pushed to the e2e job: replace `cat keyfile` with `tr -d '\r\n' < keyfile` and replaced `echo $API_KEY` with `printf '%s' "$API_KEY"` in the steps. rerunning now.
maya: FYI added a short note to our SDK README about trimming env var inputs for examples and showing the `printf` pattern.
sam: short checklist for anyone hitting this: 1) identify source of key (file vs secret manager) 2) trim CR/LF when exporting 3) when base64-ing, ensure single line 4) in Docker/GHA, use `printf -n` or `tr -d` 5) if still failing, `curl -v` to inspect header.
nina: thanks all — rerun passed on the new job. leaving the README note and small CI fix. :thumbsup:
